market_question: Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $120 by end of June?
reasoning: Silver reaching $120/oz by mid-2026 would require a >3.7x increase from current ~$32 in just over a year—far exceeding its all-time high of ~$50. Even under extreme inflationary or supply-shock scenarios, a rally of this magnitude is vanishingly unlikely. The market's 6.8% implied probability massively overestimates tail risk, making 'No' a strong sell.
evidence_points: Silver's all-time high is ~$50 (1980 and 2011), so $120 is uncharted territory and more than double that peak.
CME silver futures active-month settlement has never exceeded $50, making a jump to $120 unprecedented.
Current fundamentals and major bank forecasts (e.g., JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs) project silver in the $30–$40 range through 2026, not beyond $50.
To hit $120, silver would need an instantaneous or sustained >275% rally from today, a move that would be historic even for volatile commodities.
sources_consulted: Current COMEX silver futures price data (SI front month ~$32 as of early 2025)
CME Group settlement methodology and active-month definition
Institutional commodity forecasts (JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs 2025-2026 outlooks)
